title: Follow-up of patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy by multi-modality imaging
summary:
Transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is characterized by the deposition of misfolded proteins in the myocardium, which leads to progressive restriction and consequently to heart failure. According to the latest study findings, wild-type ATTR (wATTR) is the most common cause of heart failure with preserved pumping function (HFpEF); less common is a hereditary form of ATTR-CM (hATTR), which is caused by a mutation in the TTR gene. In addition to conventional drug therapy for heart failure, so-called "targeted" therapies have recently become available. For ATTR-CM, this is possible in the form of a transthyretin stabilizer (Tafamidis, Vyndaquel). In the approval study, a decrease in mortality and a reduction in hospitalizations was demonstrated. However, it is currently unclear how exactly patients should be followed up and to what extent it is possible to detect a non-response or progression of the pathology at an early stage. At the Charité Berlin Amyloidosis Center (ACCB), patients with various amyloidoses are treated on an interdisciplinary basis. The majority of these patients suffer from wtATTR-CM and regularly present to the ACCB as part of their clinical routine. 
The prospective observational study presented here aims to follow up patients with ATTR-CM under tafamidis therapy using multi-modality imaging in routine clinical practice. The main focus will be on cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR). By evaluating quantitative markers of this method, such as T1 and T2 relaxation times based on parametric sequences, possible predictors of the course of therapy are to be investigated. The FAITH study will be conducted at all 4 Charité campuses. In addition, the results will be considered multimodally and analyzed with data from the existing registry and clinic, such as echocardiographic, clinical and laboratory data.

interventions.name: Patients with confirmed ATTR-CM who receive a cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging examination before starting therapy with tafamidis and 9 and 18 months after starting therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Diagnosed ATTR-CM according to current standards (TTE, DPD-scintigraphy and/or biopsy) AND:
2.	Eligible to receive treatment with Tafamidis 
3.	Informed consent
4.	Agrees to receive note about incidental findings
5.	Valid health insurance
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Non ATTR-CM
2.	Severe cardiovascular comorbidities including:
a.	Myocardial infarction within the last 6 months
b.	After coronary stenting with in the last 6 month
c.	After coronary artery bypass graft (CABG)
d.	Permanent atrial fibrillation
3.	Absolute contraindications for CMR
4.	Allergy against gadolinium-containing contrast agent
5.	Chronic kidney insufficiency with a GFR <30 ml/min
6.	Pregnancy/Breastfeeding
7.	No consent to study
